security_spec.violation_condition: In FreeBSD's bhyve IOMMU GPA second-stage translation (or future RISC-V IOMMU driver), when a superpage mapping (2MB/1GB Sv39x4/Sv48x4 hgatp entry) spans a guest-physical range that overlaps a virtual interrupt file region (msiptp.MODE != MSIPTP_Off with active msi_addr_mask/pattern), and the IOMMU proceeds with the superpage granularity instead of reducing gst_page_sz to the largest sub-page that avoids the overlap—allowing the DMA write to bypass MSI page-table remapping and land directly as an unmediated memory access into the VIF region
security_spec.summary: IOMMU GPA superpage overlapping virtual interrupt file region silently bypasses MSI interrupt remapping, letting an assigned PCIe device inject arbitrary MSIs into a bhyve guest VM

findings.finding: pmap_ps_enabled(pmap_t pmap __unused) ignores its pmap parameter entirely and returns the global superpages_enabled tunable. This means stage-2 (hgatp) pmaps in bhyve will also have superpage promotion enabled. If a future RISC-V IOMMU driver and MSIPTP/VIF infrastructure were added, 2MB hgatp superpage entries could span guest-physical ranges that overlap virtual interrupt file regions, allowing DMA writes to bypass MSI page-table remapping. Currently benign because no RISC-V IOMMU driver, MSIPTP CSR, or msi_addr_mask infrastructure exists in the FreeBSD RISC-V port.

hgatp is written with pmap->pm_satp at VM entry, preceded by hfence_gvma() as required by the RISC-V spec (Section 5.3.2). No IOMMU involvement in this path — the hgatp CSR governs CPU-side second-stage translation only. DMA/IOMMU translation uses a separate IOMMU page-table root, which does not exist for RISC-V in this codebase.

Stage-2 pmap initialization correctly calls pmap_pinit_stage(pmap, PM_STAGE2). No IOMMU context is associated with this pmap — the stage-2 mapping is purely for CPU-side G-stage translation via hgatp. No DMA remapping or VIF overlap logic is needed at this layer absent an IOMMU.

The VM_MEMMAP_F_IOMMU flag is referenced only under #ifdef guard, and this macro is defined exclusively in sys/amd64/include/vmm_dev.h — it is not defined for RISC-V builds. The IOMMU memory-map tracking path is entirely compiled out on riscv, confirming that no GPA-to-IOMMU-page-table translation path exists for RISC-V guests.

pmap_promote_l2 promotes 512 contiguous 4KB L3 PTEs into a 2MB L2 superpage. The only gate is pmap_ps_enabled(pmap), which unconditionally returns true for all pmap types including stage-2. In a stage-2 (hgatp) pmap, this creates GPA superpage mappings. If a future RISC-V IOMMU driver were to share or mirror the hgatp page tables (as some architectures do), a 2MB GPA superpage could span a VIF region boundary, granting DMA the ability to write into MSI-redirection memory as plain memory. Currently no IOMMU exists to exploit this, but the promotion path has no awareness of potential VIF overlap.
